editorial:
Imagine you are stuck in a small town with a lounge singer who thinks he is a huge star but is actually just a flirt. That is how you enter the wild world of this comedy. You get to follow Dino, a guy who loves the spotlight, as he gets tricked into staying overnight by two guys who desperately want him to sing their songs. To keep things from getting awkward, they hire a local girl to pretend to be the wife of one of the partners. It is a goofy, high-energy setup that feels like a classic stage play where everything that can go wrong eventually does.

What really works here is the funny chemistry between the characters and the fast dialogue. While some of the jokes feel a bit dated, the pacing keeps you moving along quickly. You will love the way the lies pile up until the characters can barely keep track of them. If you want a lighthearted night, you should try renting it on Apple TV or adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection for a crisp picture. It is a perfect choice if you like old-school humor and quirky characters who get in over their heads.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the lies finally catch up to everyone. After a chaotic night of pretending, the truth comes out about the fake marriage and the scheme to get Dino to sing. Dino realizes he was being used, but the movie wraps up with a sense of irony. The characters find a weird kind of peace with their failures, and the credits roll after the music and the madness finally settle down.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Hollywood comedies and funny misunderstandings.
